samples.summary: Published API reference still documents the old freeze bound and merge rules this change narrows. `packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md:650-651` states `rows` is `integer 0..1000000` and `cols` `0..18278`, but `parseFreeze` now rejects anything above `MaxSnappedFreeze` (1,000) with a 400; line 653 says `GET`/`PUT` return `{rows, cols}` without noting that `PUT freeze` may now answer with a *snapped* boundary different from the one requested; the merges rule table at 688-694 lists only the per-span 100,000 cap and gains neither the new `MaxMergeEntries` (10,000) nor `MaxMergeCoveredCells` (1e6) 400s nor the new 409 for a map that straddles the tab's freeze. An external client following the shipped docs now gets 400/409 on requests the docs call legal, and a previously-valid `{"rows": 5000}` call breaks silently at the doc level.

`MaxSnappedFreeze` is applied as a *request* cap only in the backend validator (`parseFreeze`), while `Sheet.setFreezePane` (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:543) passes a caller-requested boundary through untouched and bounds only the snap's growth. That is precisely the asymmetry this change's own rationale condemns for merges ("a cap only this writer honored would let the other two grow a map this wholesale replace could never express again"): the editor / a store write / an import can leave `frozenRows` above 1,000, and the v1 API then 400s on any attempt to set or restore that same value, with no per-axis alternative. Either the engine should refuse/clamp a requested depth past the paintable ceiling too, or the validator should not restate a bound the engine declines to enforce.

`docs/design/rest-api.md` §5.4 is the design-level record of these endpoints and still says the only 409 on `POST .../move` is the merge-split refusal, and that "each endpoint echoes back the request it applied". The change adds a second 409 (a reorder parking a merged block across the freeze) and makes `POST insert` / `POST delete` silently grow `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` via the new snap in `shiftWorksheetViewState`, neither of which is recorded there — the new API behavior is documented only inside the nested `docs/design/sheets/sheet.md` (lines 129-145), which is not where the repo files the REST contract and is not covered by the top-level backtick-path check.

`docs/design/frontend.md`'s YorkieStore method table still describes `setMerge(anchor, span)` as "Write to `root.sheets[tabId].merges[anchorSref]`". After this change the frontend store spends a merge budget, may refuse the write, and returns a boolean the engine keys its in-memory map on — a `Store` contract change the doc that documents that store does not record (the `Store` interface excerpt in sheets/sheet.md was updated, frontend.md was not).
searchedFor: grep setMerge across packages for other Store implementations

samples.summary: The straddle check is written out twice in the backend: `assertMergesClearOfFreeze` here and `assertMoveKeepsMergesOffFreeze` in worksheet-structure.controller.ts:180 are the same loop (`toMergeRange(parseRef(sref), span)` → `crossesFreezePane` → throw `ConflictException`) over a merge map, differing only in where the map comes from and the message. Given the change's own stated goal of one implementation per invariant, a shared `findMergeCrossingFreeze(merges, rows, cols)` in `model/worksheet/merging.ts` (beside `crossesFreezePane`) would keep the two controllers from drifting on which blocks count as straddling.

Scope breadth: this single change bundles at least five separable concerns — the merge-map budget (new caps + enforcement in five writers + a defensive clamp on load), the freeze/merge straddle invariant across engine and API, merge propagation through copy/cut/paste, a change in copy-buffer lifetime (paste no longer clears it; new `revalidateCopyBuffer` keyed on axis IDs), and single-cell paste anchor normalization, plus a `rangeOf` rewrite in `model/core/coordinates.ts`. The copy-buffer lifetime change in particular is a user-visible behavior change (repeat paste, refused-paste retention) independent of merges, and the `Store.setMerge` signature change ripples through three store implementations. With no originating issue text to scope it against, this is hard to review or revert piecewise; splitting the budget work from the freeze invariant from the clipboard work would each stand alone.

verdict.reason: All four premises hold in the working tree. parseFreeze (packages/backend/src/yorkie/worksheet-settings.ts:69-75) bounds rows/cols by MaxSnappedFreeze = 1000 (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/merging.ts:60), so a previously-documented {"rows": 5000} is now a 400; PUT freeze snaps and returns the stored boundary (worksheet.controller.ts:107-133); parseMerges adds MaxMergeEntries=10000 and MaxMergeCoveredCells=1e6 400s via mergeBudgetError (worksheet-settings.ts:138-144,189-192; merging.ts:30,42,86-94); and PUT merges throws a 409 when a span straddles the freeze (worksheet.controller.ts:193-209). The published reference packages/documentation/developers/rest-api.md still says rows is `integer 0..1000000` and cols `0..18278` (650-651), still describes GET/PUT as returning {rows, cols} with no note of a snapped answer (653), and its merge rule table (688-694) stops at the per-span 100,000 cap with no entry/covered-cell caps and no 409 — the only 409s in the file are at 96, 397, 631, 821, none for merges. I searched wide for a counterexample: every *.md in the repo mentioning "freeze" is cli.md, rest-api.md, design docs or archived task notes; no OpenAPI/JSON/YAML spec documents these endpoints. docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:120-162 does document MaxSnappedFreeze, the snap, and the three merge ceilings, and cli.md:597,612 documents `sheets freeze set` with no bound, but neither is the shipped API reference, so neither refutes the claim. Blocking as major under this lens: the shipped user-facing reference advertises as legal three request shapes the server now rejects with 400/409, so the cost falls on external clients rather than on internal tidiness.

verdict.reason: The code is as described (parseFreeze caps at MaxSnappedFreeze; Sheet.setFreezePane/snapFreezePastMerges bound only growth), but it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) There is no duplication that can diverge: worksheet-settings.ts:4 imports MaxSnappedFreeze from the engine (merging.ts:60) and the snap itself is one shared implementation used by both Sheet.setFreezePane (sheet.ts:557-562) and the controller (worksheet.controller.ts:121-128). (b) The behaviour matches the canonical design doc rather than diverging from it: docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:153-155 states verbatim "Only growth is bounded — a line the caller asked for passes through untouched, since bounding the request is the validator's job (parseFreeze)." (c) The merge analogy the finding relies on is explicitly distinguished in that same rationale: the merge caps must live in the engine because PUT merges is a wholesale replace of an accumulating budget with no per-anchor form (worksheet.controller.ts:51-58, sheets/sheet.md:156-169), whereas PUT freeze is an absolute two-number write that can always express any value <=1,000 or 0, so no client is locked out of fixing a document; only re-asserting an already-unpaintable >1,000 depth is refused, which is the ceiling's stated purpose. What is left is a where-to-enforce preference with no acceptance criterion unmet and no user denied the stated outcome — minor/wrong-layer at most, which does not block; the API round-trip angle belongs to the correctness lens.
